newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen steady to soft as crude eases.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen steady to soft as crude eases.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Tuesday were expected to stay steady to shade softer as crude prices eased on healthy supplies despite firm paper quotes, traders said.
Physical 180-centistoke cargoes for October lifting were quoted at $120-$121 per tonne on Monday. Offers for October barrels were indicated at $122 per tonne but edged lower to $121 late Tuesday.
Traders expected the same major oil companies to emerge to offer October barrels. They said there are at least two strong bids expected in the market.
If the bids can take on the offers, prices may remain supported, said a trader.
Chinese demand remained weak as current prices were too high, traders said.
On the paper swaps, October was discussed at $120.25-$121.25 up from Monday's $119.50-$119.75.
Taiwan has awarded its tender to buy low sulphur fuel oil to a Japanese refiner at just under $142 per tonne for November to December delivery.
